Demos

Every figure in the corpus, drawn live from its source. The corpus is also the project’s test suite, with each figure’s compiled form checked in, and many of its figures were ported from graphs, shaders and blog figures made by other means.

Figures start drawing as they come near the screen. Controls are built from what each figure declares: a play button if anything follows time, a slider for each param, and arrows for beats. Some figures also have handles to drag.

  1. 001

    A breathing circle

    The smallest figure that exercises the whole path: an implicit curve whose radius follows time, colored on each side of its signed distance. Its second sheet bands both sides by that distance, and not a line of the figure changes.

    The squaring map

    A circle orthogonal to the unit circle, and a grid of lines over the square around it, raised to a power from 1 to 2. The circle becomes a limaçon, and the grid’s lines still cross at right angles, since the map is conformal.

  13. 013

    Rolling the strip into a tube

    The one-turn strip of the grid, with rows colored by arm, rolling up into a tube. Each row runs off the top and comes back in at the bottom as the next row of its arm, so an arm is one line wound around. Its points are in space, and the sheet fades the far side from self.z.

  15. 015

    Nearest isn’t nearest after log

    Dots at 1, e and e² on the line are evenly spaced after log, at 0, 1 and 2. Each line marks the dot nearest x by its own distance, and they disagree between e^(n+½) and (eⁿ + eⁿ⁺¹)/2, which is shaded on both. Drag x.

  16. 016

    Unwrapping the spiral

    One slider from the flat strip to the Doyle spiral, through fₜ(u) = (e^(tu) − 1)/t + 1, which keeps 1 fixed. The strip holds one circle of each period, chosen by a whole-number range; the copies a turn above and below fade as it wraps, and the rows along 1 and ω curl into arms.

    • Source on GitHub
    • Open in the playground

    unwrap.pen · theme.style · plain.style · dark.style

  17. 017

    Coloring the spiral by arm

    Each circle is colored by which row of the grid it’s on, along ω, 1 or 1 + ω, wrapped around by the number of arms, which is how many rows the period crosses. Each arm’s exact curve runs through its circles, and on the grid each arm is a straight row. Where the rows run along the period they close into rings. The second look adds the period A, which crosses one row of each arm.

    • Source on GitHub
    • Open in the playground

    arm-colors.pen · theme.style · plain.style · narrow.style · dark.style · period.style

  18. 018

    The camera in log space

    A camera at c sees the spiral times e^(−c), so in log space its square screen is a region with a wavy edge that slides by c. Steps of 1 + ω line the circles up with where they started at every whole step, and the arm colors too after p = 2; a pure zoom as far never lines up.
